newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BEATS RAFTER IN NEW HAVEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BEATS RAFTER IN NEW HAVEN FINAL.

text.p: This time there was no comeback for Patrick Rafter as top seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia quelled the eighth-seeded Australian 7-6 (7-4) 6-4 in the final of the $1.04 million Pilot Pen Sunday.

"This week has been nice to me. I couldn't ask for anything better," said Kafelnikov, ranked sixth in the world coming in but improving to third after the victory. "I won a title and this is a great way to get ready for the U.S. Open."
Rafter, ranked 18th, won over the crowd this week by surviving three successive three-set matches on the way to the final. It was his fourth final of the year, although he has yet to win a title.
"This was a good tournament for me, it helps my confidence," said Rafter. "I might not like coming in second so much, but it's better than coming in 56th, isn't it?"

Kafelnikov, who claimed the $150,000 winner's purse after winning his second title of the year, lost his service for the only time when he appeared to have the match put away with a 5-3 lead in the second set.
The Russian got into a 15-40 hole in the next game when he hit long from the baseline. Rafter then whacked a forehand return down the line for the break.

Determined not to let things go to a third set, the Russian hit two backhand passes on his opponent's approaches and suddenly, Rafter was facing match point. The Aussie staved off one with an ace, but Kafelnikov passed again on the second match point when Rafter's stretch volley went long.

Rafter, a relentless net charger, fought off three break points in the first set before forcing the tiebreaker. Kafelnikov put away an overhead for set point at 6-4 in the breaker. Rafter then netted a backhand return to end the set.
"I know his strategy was coming to the net. He figured that was the only way he could beat me," said Kafelnikov. "He couldn't do it from the baseline."
Kafelnikov broke in the second game of the second set as Rafter double-faulted in the final point. The top seed led 3-0 4-1 and 5-2 before Rafter fought back to make it close.

"Maybe I went for a little too much," said Rafter in reviewing his net-rushing tactics. "He's just so smooth, he seems not to use any energy at all. But I liked having the crowd behind me. I try to bust my guts every match."
